description:
FOUND s484c (Opus, 2026-09-14) by #1726's breaking-case probe
(scratch/s484c/probe/p1726-break.pl).  PRE-EXISTING and unchanged by #1726,
which only added the GLOB arm (a lexical handle is not a p-typeglob at all).

perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl, after `open(my $fh, '<', '/etc/hostname')`:

    $$fh{x}          perl DIED    PCL DIED     agree
    $$fh[0]          perl DIED    PCL "undef"  <-- diverges
    exists $$fh{x}   perl DIED    PCL 0        <-- diverges
    *$fh{IO}         perl def     PCL def      agree

perl's `my $fh` from a 3-arg open holds a REF to an anonymous glob, and a ref
to a glob is not a container: "Not a HASH reference" / "Not an ARRAY
reference".  PCL stores a handle object (not a p-typeglob â that is what
%p-glob-slot-of-handle exists for), and the two element resolvers
(p-ensure-arrayref / %p-designator-hash) let it fall through to their
catch-all, so the read answers undef and `exists` a quiet NO.  The HASH read
dies only because SBCL's GETHASH type-errors on it, which is the right answer
for the wrong reason.

FIX SHAPE (untried): the two resolvers `p-ensure-hashref` /
`p-ensure-arrayref` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) are the ONE place that decides what
a designator designates (#1628, #1726).  A HANDLE is a wrong referent there,
so the arm is `%p-not-a-ref` â the same answer the scalar-referent and
wrong-kind arms already give.  Check %p-wrong-referent-p first: extending
THAT predicate to know about handles may be the whole fix, and it is what the
four element primitives already consult.

BAR: the four rows above, `*$fh{IO}` and `stat *$fh{IO}` still working (task
#1047's rows), a bareword handle's `\*FH` (#1726's row 6-7, which must keep
dying), and `print $fh`/`close $fh` untouched.  A `cl/` change, so the full
sweep plus the io/ companion leg.

ADDENDUM (s484c, the full seven-row table â the probe is
scratch/s484c/probe/p1755.pl, and a `git archive edd6dc78` extraction answers
byte-identically, so every row below is PRE-EXISTING):

    spelling          perl                          PCL
    $$fh{x}           dies Not a HASH reference     dies, but with SBCL's own
                                                    text ("Value of pcl::h in
                                                    (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil)
                                                    is #<sb-sys:fd-stream ...>")
    $$fh[0]           dies Not an ARRAY reference   undef            <- SILENT
    exists $$fh{x}    dies Not a HASH reference     0                <- SILENT
    exists $$fh[0]    dies Not an ARRAY reference   0                <- SILENT
    delete $$fh{x}    dies Not a HASH reference     dies, SBCL's text
    $$fh{x} = 1       dies Not a HASH reference     dies, SBCL's text
    $$fh[0] = 1       dies Not an ARRAY reference   "wrote"          <- SILENT

So the family is FOUR silent-wrong answers, not two, and the fourth is a
WRITE that succeeds into a handle.  The three that do die leak SBCL's type
error into `$@`, where perl's message is short and trappable â so the arm
this task asks for must also carry perl's wording, exactly as #1726's
glob-REF arm does.  (Task #1755 was filed for this and is FOLDED here; that
id is unused.)
subject: a LEXICAL filehandle in element position answers undef/0 where perl dies: `$$fh{x}` and `exists $$fh{x}` after `open my $fh`
